subject: Prompt collection & model fit follow-up - ACME
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt collection & model fit follow-up - ACME

Hi Jane,

Thanks for the convo earlier - great to learn more about ACME's customer support use case and the SLA targets you mentioned (95th pct under 400ms for short completions, daily retention requirements). Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Model recommendations: based on the examples you shared, we think starting with redwood-3b-q4f for the majority of routing (cost-sensitive, short replies) and redwood-7b-enc for longer-context summarization/backfill makes sense. If you need higher-quality open-response generation for low-volume, consider redwood-13b.
- Benchmarks: attached is a link to our internal ACME benchmark run (small sample) and the public eval harness we use for conversational/QA coverage. See links below.
- Prompt collection: can you share a seed set of customer prompts across the categories we discussed (FAQ, complex support threads, edge cases like billing + PII redaction)? CSV or simple text is fine. We need 100-300 prompts to build a representative eval set.
- Redaction guidance: if any prompts contain PII/PHI, please flag and we can walk through our recommended redaction patterns. We can also accept a redacted and an original (secure upload to your S3) if procurement requires.
- Next steps: if you email the seed prompts (or upload to the Drive link), Rafael (cc'd) and I will run a quick model-fit eval and share a short report + recommended prompt tweaks by EOD next Tue (7/28).

Attachments (referenced): acme_prompt_samples.csv (template), redaction_guidance.pdf

Links: https://redwood.inference/evals/ACME-benchmarks-2026  

Thanks - look forward to the prompt set.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

---
Note: We recommend providing a few examples of expected outputs per prompt (gold responses) where possible to speed evaluation and help catch quality regressions.

Hi Marissa - thanks for the summary.

I'm attaching a first pass (acme_prompt_samples.csv) with 40 seed prompts across FAQ and billing flows. A couple notes:
- Some prompts contain customer identifiers (order numbers, email snippets). We can either redact or provide a mapping file. Procurement prefers minimal PII in shared files.
- Reporting/metrics folks asked whether you can surface token-level latency breakdowns per model in the evaluation report.

We'll upload the full prompt set to the Drive folder by next Tuesday as you suggested. Can you confirm where to send any restricted files (SFTP or private S3)? Also please include a lightweight guide on expected labeling/expected outputs - that will help our CS team produce gold responses.

Thanks,
Jane
Senior Product Manager, ACME Corp

Attachment: acme_prompt_samples.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt collection & model fit follow-up - ACME

Hi Jane - got the CSV, thanks. Rafael and I reviewed the seed prompts quickly. Quick answers to your asks: 

- Secure upload: we can accept PII via an encrypted S3 upload (we'll send a presigned upload link) or a short-lived SFTP endpoint. I'll have our security ops send the S3 presigned URL once procurement signs the DPA/LOA.
- Latency breakdowns: absolutely - we'll include token-level latency and cost estimates per model in the short report. That's helpful for your infra/cost decisioning.
- Labeling guide: attaching a short redaction + labeling guidance doc (redaction_guidance.pdf). Couple tips in the doc: replace identifiers with <ORDER_ID>, remove full names unless necessary, and mark any PHI fields explicitly. If you can provide 3-5 gold outputs per prompt (one-line expected answer or a short summary), our evals will score much better and surface quality regressions.

Action items: 
1) We'll run the quick model-fit eval on the 40 sample prompts and share initial findings + recommended model routing (redwood-3b-q4f vs redwood-7b-enc) by EOD Tue.
2) Please confirm upload method for any PII and whether procurement will need a separate procurement contact.

-R
Marissa

Attachment: redaction_guidance.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt collection & model fit follow-up - ACME

Looping in some technical notes from our quick pass.

- Quality/regression concerns: I noticed a couple of prompts in the sample where the expected output is short but models tend to over-generate (this will affect latency and token-cost). We'll flag these in the report and recommend explicit stop tokens and stronger instruction prefixes.
- Eval plan: we'll run the seed set through redwood-3b-q4f, redwood-7b-enc, and a small redwood-13b run for a quality baseline. We'll produce per-prompt metrics (exact-match where applicable, BLEU/ROUGE for summarization, and a human-rated quality score for ambiguity cases).
- Attaching interim benchmark_results.md with a small QA table from the quick runs - it's preliminary but will help procurement understand tradeoffs.

If ACME has any edge-case threads (multi-turn with code snippets, attachments, or non-English content), please include them in the upload - they catch regressions.

-Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: benchmark_results.md
